work_or_witness: Chapter 1, 'An Empty Road,' official excerpt; The Eye of the World printed witness
canonical_term: the Wheel of Time and the Pattern
literal_gloss: cyclical Ages and the woven order of events
definition: The novel's cyclic cosmological frame in which Ages recur and lives/events are understood through a Pattern rather than a linear one-time history.
cultural_caution: Do not reduce the Wheel/Pattern to a timeline mechanic, deterministic game engine, or character node; Book One interpretations differ among characters.

citations.locator: Chapter 1, 'An Empty Road,' official excerpt; The Eye of the World printed witness
supports: The opening establishes recurring Ages and the Wheel's cyclic frame.

work_or_witness: The Eye of the World, Chapters 2–10, 21–23, and 45–53 printed witness; official synopsis
canonical_term: the One Power; saidin and saidar
literal_gloss: the world's channeling power, understood through distinct male/female halves
definition: A source-specific cosmological power accessed by channeling, with gendered halves, historical danger, bodily cost, institutions, and contested knowledge that structure the book's fears and possibilities.
cultural_caution: Not a generic mana pool, spell list, elemental system, or binary gender game mechanic. Terminology and social implications must remain source-specific.

citations.locator: The Eye of the World, Chapters 2–10, 21–23, and 45–53 printed witness; official synopsis
supports: Moiraine, Egwene, Nynaeve, and Rand's Book One power context is central to the flight and Eye crisis.

work_or_witness: The Eye of the World, Chapters 2–10 printed witness; official synopsis
literal_gloss: the organized women channelers represented here by Moiraine
definition: A source-specific organization, social category, and political reputation connected to channeling; Moiraine is an individual member, while the collective is not a node.
cultural_caution: Do not equate Aes Sedai with generic witches, mages, a uniform faction, or an automatic moral alignment. Local fear and internal distinctions are not flattened.

citations.locator: The Eye of the World, Chapters 2–10 printed witness; official synopsis
supports: Moiraine's Aes Sedai identity provokes the travelers' initial fear and is central to the flight.

work_or_witness: The Eye of the World, Chapters 2–10 printed witness
literal_gloss: the Aes Sedai–Warder relation exemplified by Moiraine and Lan
definition: A source-specific bonded relation that links Aes Sedai and Warder service, perception, protection, and vulnerability in the Moiraine–Lan pair.
cultural_caution: Do not treat the bond as a summon, companion slot, marriage, ownership relation, or combat buff; consent, duty, and cost remain contextual.

citations.locator: The Eye of the World, Chapters 2–10 printed witness
supports: Moiraine and Lan's named Aes Sedai/Warder partnership demonstrates the term in Book One.

work_or_witness: The Eye of the World, Chapters 36–40 and 45–53 printed witness
literal_gloss: a person around whom the Pattern bends events
definition: The Book One term for unusual Pattern-centered influence, invoked around the young travelers without making it a complete identity or deterministic destiny explanation.
cultural_caution: Do not map ta'veren to a chosen-one class, plot armor, leadership statistic, or universal fate mechanic. Its operation and implications are contested and incomplete here.

citations.locator: The Eye of the World, Chapters 36–40 and 45–53 printed witness
supports: The Pattern-centered significance of the travelers becomes a stated Book One concern.

work_or_witness: The Eye of the World, Chapters 5–10 printed witness; official synopsis
literal_gloss: Shadow creatures and their named categories pursuing the Two Rivers group
definition: Source-native Shadow being categories whose attack on Emond's Field and pursuit initiate the novel's flight; individual creatures are not promoted to collective nodes.
cultural_caution: Do not turn these categories into generic beastfolk, monster races, or an enemy encounter table. They are bound to the novel's Shadow cosmology and fear politics.

citations.locator: The Eye of the World, Chapters 5–10 printed witness; official synopsis
supports: Trolloc/Myrddraal attack and pursuit force the young travelers to flee.

work_or_witness: The Eye of the World, Chapters 45–53 printed witness; official title/series record
literal_gloss: the guarded destination/resource of the Book One quest
definition: A source-specific guarded destination and concentrated-power context around which the novel's final party and Shadow confrontation occurs.
cultural_caution: The Eye is not a character, mana cache, quest reward, or reusable artifact classification. Its meaning is deliberately bound to the Book One climax.

citations.locator: The Eye of the World, Chapters 45–53 printed witness; official title/series record
